answer: Nearest-neighbor distance for each of the 45,433 LA County 2023 footprints (wildfire_la layer) was computed in ArcGIS Pro with Near(buildings, buildings) in NAD83 UTM 11N (planar, metres, edge to edge). Near on one class against itself skips the feature's own OID: 0 self-matches, and every footprint got a neighbor. Median 2.20 m, mean 3.91 m, p25 0.95 m, p75 4.11 m, p95 12.30 m, max 1303.6 m. 6,811 footprints (15.0%) have distance 0 because they touch or overlap another footprint (none are duplicate geometries or share a BLD_ID), so 0 means attached, not a self-match.
traps_or_caveats: Self-match avoided: Near of a layer to itself ignores the same OID. Verified 0 rows with NEAR_FID == own OID; no duplicate BLD_IDs or identical geometries.

15% of distances are exactly 0 (touching or overlapping footprints, e.g. attached units or house plus garage); edge-to-edge distance, not centroid distance. Centroid distance or merging touching footprints would give a different spacing measure.
Layer holds Courtyard (289) and Free Standing Solar Structure (76) codes alongside Building; these are counted as footprints/neighbors. Filtering them out would change some NN values.

Layer is clipped to 1/4 mile around the fire perimeters, so footprints near the clip edge may have a true neighbor outside the layer; large distances (max 1.3 km, 50 over 100 m) are partly edge or open-land artifacts and unreliable near the boundary.
Planar distance in UTM 11N metres, not geodesic; negligible error at this scale.
Distances are 2023 pre-fire footprints; the result says nothing about damage by itself (about one third of footprints have no DINS record, not 'undamaged').
